chapter: Zach White, Cotton Pickers and Cab Calloway
title: Recording 'Moonglow' and the solo that gave him a nickname
summary: To fill out a record date Cab had Barefield solo on 'Moonglow'. Heard later on a loudspeaker he thought it was Benny Carter; musicians nicknamed him Moonglow and copied the solo.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Right. And then before we went to Europe we made a recording session. And you know in those days you always recorded in sets of fours. So we went down that day and we only had three sides to do and we didn't have a fourth side. And Cab, most all the things -- in fact, all the things we recorded then were vocals, mostly with the band. Solos fit in here and there. But he didn't have a fourth side so in the meantime Will Hudson (PHONETIC) had brought us one chorus arranged on "Moonglow" to the Cotton Club and we had played it, so we used to use it as a sign-off. So Cab said, well, we've got to record another side to fill out the session, so I'll tell you what we'll do. I don't think Mills is going to release it but we'll do Moonglow. And he said, we'll play the chorus like we have it and then, Eddie Barefield, you take the second chorus as a solo and then we'll come back and do a little out chorus.

We did that one take and walked out of the studio and went to Europe. After we came back from Europe we were down in Texas. And we heard this record playing, you know, they always played records before the dance over the loud speaker. And we heard this saxophone playing and I said, gee. Everybody stopped and listened to the saxophone and everybody was trying to figure out who it was. And I said, gee, it

sounds like Benny Carter, you know.
So we go in and I asked the man, who was that playing that? He said, don't you know your own records? He said, it's "Moonglow" by Cab Calloway. Then I had to buy the record to learn the solo off it so we could do it on stage. That was the first instrumental Cab had recorded at that time. So they featured me on the stage with this.
You more or less played it the same?
Yes. Well, I had to learn it.
But people wanted to hear it exactly as it was on the record?
So the musicians nicknamed me "Moonglow" at that time and all the musicians, saxophone players, copied that solo. Even Lionel Hampton used to play it on the VIBES.

Yeah. And then that became a famous solo amongst the musicians, like Coleman Hawkins brought in Soul "Became" at that time. In fact, we did it on there the other day. And even Charlie Parker and all of them years later copied that solo, you know.
